t: Antić and Papić are one family, and a by-name explains it
s: The two surnames never interleave in 15,643 people. They touch at one man — and the 1806 Vrbnik register underlines Papa as the household's nadimak.

t: A man born after his own granddaughter
s: Caetano Bacchi is dated 1779; his daughter's daughter was born in 1781. Two years cannot hold two generations, and two more ancestors go with it.

t: Two Žubrinić couples of the same two names, a generation apart
s: One tree couple is given sons born 1834 and 1880. A Senj marriage of 1910 names the later son's parents in the same words — so the tree has merged two men.

t: Hedviga sang at the Hotel Therapia, and it is still standing
s: The only thing anyone has ever said about what she did. The hotel opened at Crikvenica in 1895 and was renamed Kvarner Palace in 2013 — the family believed it had closed.

t: Twenty-two years of her life are missing
s: Senj in April 1953, South Africa in April 1975 — and an entire country in between, known from two words on a later record.

t: The Latin case-endings were the priests, not a transcriber
s: One hand at Karlobag writes Nomen Joannis Georgij in 1777 and nomen Oliva Maria in 1781. Scribal caprice, not error — and the ending tells you which record the person came out of.

t: Four sorting buckets were being published as ancestors
s: “1800-1830 Birth — Selce Papić (Papa)” and three like it had person pages and children attached. Found by a new self-consistency check.

t: Smokvica 114 is a zadruga, not a household
s: A control document puts a first cousin at the same number. The house places Juraj in Ilija's kin-group; it cannot name his father.
